Senses.PreferredTarget: sink into emptiness and stick in stillness
AlternateTargets: sink in emptiness and remain stuck in stillness
sink into the empty and stagnate in stillness
Senses.Explanation: A paired critical verb phrase: "sink into" (沈) "emptiness" (空) and "stick or stagnate in" (滯) "stillness" (寂), attested in this graph form 9 times in 9 allowlisted texts. The Chinese Chan sources use it to identify a failure, not to name an activity they commend. Fozhi Duanyu sets two obstructions against each other: "if one teaching exists, layer upon layer of iron walls and silver mountains; if the myriad teachings are absent, everywhere one sinks into emptiness and sticks in stillness" (一法若有重重鐵壁銀山，萬法若無處處沈空滯寂). Gaofeng includes the phrase among a long series of proposed reasons for failure, asking, "is it sinking into emptiness and sticking in stillness?" (莫是沈空滯寂麼), before rejecting the whole diagnostic list as the answer. Yuansou says figures in an arhat painting "sink into emptiness and stick in stillness, know only their own completion, and do not attend to delivering living beings" (沈空滯寂，只知自了，不顧度生). Chushi explicitly calls it "the Chan illness of the two vehicles" (二乘禪病).
Senses.Note: The first graph also appears as the common variant "sink" (沉): "sink into emptiness and stick in stillness" (沉空滯寂) occurs 30 times in 21 allowlisted texts. The assigned form with "sink" (沈) remains the headword because it is independently attested across nine texts. Both spellings are condemnatory in the sampled Chan contexts; neither names anything the speakers recommend.

Occurrences.Kwic: 萬法若無處處沈空滯寂。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: 續傳燈錄, Yuwang Duanyu section. Yuwang Duanyu is the exact speaker: in his own instruction he contrasts positing one dharma as iron walls and silver mountains with positing no dharmas and everywhere sinking into emptiness and stagnating in quiescence.
Gaofeng asks among a long diagnostic series, "is it sinking into emptiness and sticking in stillness?" He then says none of the proposed faults is the answer.

Occurrences.Kwic: 惟其沈空滯寂，只知自了
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Yuansou's caption on an arhat painting says, "they only sink into emptiness and stick in stillness, knowing only their own completion."

Occurrences.Kwic: 若也沈空滯寂，墮於二乘禪病。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Chushi says, "if one sinks into emptiness and sticks in stillness, one falls into the Chan illness of the two vehicles."

Occurrences.Kwic: 沈空滯寂及自知名無學聲聞
Occurrences.AttributionNote: 古尊宿語錄, Baizhang Huaihai's second recorded discourse. Baizhang Huaihai is the exact speaker throughout the extended teaching turn, including his statement that sinking into emptiness, stagnating in quiescence, and knowing this oneself is called an adept beyond training.
